title: Room-to-Room Temperature Imbalance
dataSources: Zigbee2MQTT device reports (`zigbee2mqtt:device`), Shelly/Tasmota telemetry (`shelly:status`, `tasmota:sensor`), Hue bridge events (`hue:event`), Nest/Ecobee thermostat (`ecobee:thermostat`), door/leak/motion sensors.
app: Philips Hue, smart plugs (Tasmota/Shelly/TP-Link Kasa), thermostats (Nest/Ecobee), locks, and Zigbee/Z-Wave sensors via MQTT / Zigbee2MQTT and HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=zigbee2mqtt:device sensor_type=temperature
| stats latest(temp_c) as temp_c by room
| eventstats max(temp_c) as hottest, min(temp_c) as coldest
| eval spread=round(hottest-coldest,1)
| where spread>4
| sort - temp_c
description: Compares the latest room temperatures and points out when one part of the house is noticeably hotter or colder than the rest.
value: Comfort complaints usually start with one room, not the whole house; a live temperature spread metric helps you balance vents, doors, and schedules.
implementation: Forward room-level temperature readings; refresh a dashboard that highlights the current warmest, coldest, and total spread.
visualization: Current-state table of room temperatures with overall spread.
grandmaExplanation: It spots how uneven the temperatures are around your home so you can spot the one room that feels wrong.
